aAbout: Argos Atlas is a hosted real-time world map that aggregates already-open official feeds — above all public cameras, which it claims number over 200,000 from official portals in more than 190 countries — and paints everything that moves around them on one flat map: flights, ships, war frontlines, verified events, infrastructure, earthquakes, fires and prediction markets. The live map is free with a free account; ARGOS PRO adds recording, history, an AI analyst layer and a 3D globe mode.
aStrengths: Argos Atlas is the broader live atlas: an order of magnitude more cameras (its claim), live flights and ships alongside the weather, camera recording with a 24-hour scrubbable archive, flight and ship history (7–90 days), sanctions and dark-vessel flags, verified frontlines and events, and geofence alerts. It asks nothing of your computer — a free account in any browser — and its team plans (up to 10 seats on DIVISION) aim it at newsrooms and analysts, not just weather watchers.
bAbout: Zoom Earth, by Neave Interactive, is a free interactive weather map and real-time hurricane tracker for the web, iOS and Android. It shows live satellite imagery updated every 10 minutes from NOAA GOES, JMA Himawari and EUMETSAT Meteosat geostationary satellites, HD imagery updated twice a day from NASA's Aqua and Terra, a real-time rain radar with nowcasting, forecast-model maps for rain, wind, temperature and pressure, hurricane tracking and a wildfire heat-spots overlay. It is a weather and satellite specialist — it has no camera network, flight or ship tracking.
bStrengths: Zoom Earth is the deeper weather specialist: near-real-time satellite imagery every 10 minutes, HD twice-daily passes, rain radar with nowcasting, full forecast-model maps (DWD ICON and NOAA GFS), best-in-class hurricane tracking drawn from NHC, JTWC, NRL and IBTrACS, and wildfire heat spots from NASA FIRMS. It is free with no account required for basic use, and its focused design beats any generalist atlas for storm depth.
betterAnswer: They overlap only on the weather. Argos Atlas is a hosted live atlas built around camera scale (200,000+ claimed), live flights and ships, recording, history and verification layers, with weather as one layer among many. Zoom Earth is a free weather specialist built around the sky itself — 10-minute satellite imagery, radar, forecast models and hurricane tracking in unmatched depth. If you watch storms, open Zoom Earth; if you monitor the world around the storm, open Argos Atlas.

intro: Argos Atlas and Zoom Earth both call themselves live world maps — and they watch completely different worlds. Argos Atlas is a hosted live atlas built around the ground: a flat map claiming 200,000+ public cameras, with live flights, ships, frontlines, verified events and prediction markets layered around them, free with a free account. Zoom Earth, by Neave Interactive, is a free weather specialist built around the sky: live satellite imagery every 10 minutes, rain radar, forecast maps and a best-in-class hurricane tracker. One monitors everything that moves; the other watches the weather above it.
pricingA: The live atlas is free and, in Argos's words, 'will stay free' — it asks for a free account and shows ads with camera limits. ARGOS PRO (EUR, VAT included in the EU/UK) lists OUTPOST at €15.99/month or €44.99 for 12 months, DISTRICT at €56.99/month or €134.99 for 12 months, DIVISION at €199/month or €809 for 12 months, and AGENCY at €1,049.99/month for registered companies. First-month welcome discounts apply to OUTPOST and DISTRICT; there is no free trial.
pricingB: Free on the web and in the iOS/Android apps, with an optional Zoom Earth Pro subscription sold through the app stores. The official App Store listing shows Pro at $1.99 and $11.99, but does not label which billing period each price corresponds to — the period for each is unverified, and there is no separate pricing page on zoom.earth itself. No free trial for Pro was stated on the official pages checked.

verdictA: Choose Argos Atlas if you want a ready-to-open working map with the biggest claimed camera catalogue, live flights and ships, recording, history and alerts — and you're willing to pay for the memory features.
verdictB: Choose Zoom Earth if you watch the weather — tracking a hurricane's approach, a storm line on radar, or smoke drifting from a wildfire, with satellite imagery minutes old and no account needed.
verdictLine: Argos Atlas is the ground truth attempt — a hosted camera-first atlas for everything moving on the surface. Zoom Earth is the sky specialist — a free weather map for everything moving above it. For storms, Zoom Earth goes deeper; for the world the storm is hitting, Argos goes wider.
worldEye: If Argos's account wall and ads are the friction there, and Zoom Earth's weather-only scope is the limit there, WorldEye is the middle path: a hosted 3D globe that opens free in any browser with no signup at all — 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view, so you can watch a storm on the map and then open a live camera inside it. It doesn't record cameras like Argos or match Zoom Earth's 10-minute satellite cadence and radar depth, and its Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) buys an OSINT toolkit and intel feeds rather than camera archives.
